motif: Resolution of conflicting attribution of 'remarkable in its exactness' phrase characterizing Joe Nickell's 1982 Nazca condor reconstruction
culture_notes: This record documents the bibliographic resolution of a misattribution, not the Nazca lines themselves.
source_type: Scientific American department column; Skeptical Inquirer peer-feature
evidence_class_notes: Strong bibliographic candidate; direct inspection of Scientific American p.84 is still pending.

alien_or_modern_reinterpretation.reinterpretation_claim: The Nickell reconstruction image, as published, was characterized as 'remarkable in its exactness' — the attribution has been incorrectly transferred to National Geographic in some fringe sources
alien_or_modern_reinterpretation.first_known_publication: Scientific American 248(6) p.84 (June 1983) 'The Big Picture' column
alien_or_modern_reinterpretation.notes: Wikipedia 'Nazca lines' article cites the June 1983 Scientific American table of contents; the original 'Big Picture' text is short and uncredited.

media_contamination_variables: Misattribution propagation: National Geographic is a familiar name and is often incorrectly cited as the source of skeptical replication coverage
Original Skeptical Inquirer text names Scientific American in the same article
National Geographic covered Nazca independently in 1975 (Loren McIntyre) and 1952 (Frank M. Setzler) but did not cover the Nickell reconstruction

expected_traces_if_true: A National Geographic 1982-1983 article using 'remarkable in its exactness'
A National Geographic byline or photo credit referencing the Kentucky reconstruction
A National Geographic issue index entry matching the claim
observed_traces: Scientific American vol. 248 no. 6 (June 1983) table of contents and 'Big Picture' column p. 84 are archived at the Wayback Machine
Nickell's own Skeptical Inquirer article credits Scientific American
No National Geographic 1982-1983 coverage of the Kentucky reconstruction has been located
negative_evidence.absence_significance: The absence of any National Geographic coverage of the Nickell reconstruction indicates the misattribution is a downstream error in secondary sources (notably the Foerster essay hosted at grahamhancock.com, which has been widely re-copied).

last_major_mutation: 1990s fringe-source misattribution to National Geographic, first appearing in pseudo-archaeological web essays

sources.citation: Nickell, Joe. 'The Nazca Drawings Revisited: Creation of a Full-Sized Duplicate.' Skeptical Inquirer vol. 7, no. 3 (Spring 1983): 36–44.
sources.notes: The Patina article archive is a third-party scanned copy of the Skeptical Inquirer piece. The article contains an explicit reference to Scientific American characterizing the work as 'remarkable in its exactness'.

Wayback-archived table-of-contents entry; full text of 'The Big Picture' department is not exposed in the SciAm open archive but the page reference is confirmed by the Nickell Skeptical Inquirer article.

sources.citation: Wikipedia contributors. 'Nazca lines.' Wikipedia, The Free Encyclopedia. (Last accessed 2026-07-12.)
sources.notes: Wikipedia cites the Scientific American 248(6) p. 84 reference with archive URL.

agent_tasks: Acquire the full text of Scientific American 248(6) (June 1983) p. 84 via HathiTrust or Internet Archive to confirm the exact wording 'remarkable in its exactness' is verbatim and not paraphrased
Document the chain of fringe-source misattribution to National Geographic (first appearance appears to be the Foerster essay at grahamhancock.com, c. 2014)
notes: Resolution of a previously unresolved attribution conflict. Companion misattribution record is recommended as a separate negative-evidence record.

publication_truth.statement: Nickell published the reconstruction report in Skeptical Inquirer and Scientific American indexed a related Big Picture item in June 1983.
publication_truth.notes: Scientific American full page text remains to be acquired.

historical_claim_truth.statement: Later sources attribute the phrase to National Geographic.
historical_claim_truth.notes: The attribution exists as a documented downstream claim.

factual_truth.statement: Scientific American, not National Geographic, appears to be the correct venue, pending direct inspection of page 84.
factual_truth.notes: Do not upgrade to A until the original page is inspected.
